_comment: FIN-002 monthly cost ceilings per environment, in USD, compared against an Infracost breakdown's projects[].breakdown.totalMonthlyCost. THIS FILE IS THE ENFORCED SOURCE: run.sh passes `--data policy` on every conftest invocation, which exposes the top-level keys below as data.dev / data.prod, and policy/finops.rego reads them through STATIC references (data.dev, data.prod) - a dynamic data[env] is a compile error inside package main. `opa test policy tests` loads this file as data the same way, so the unit tests read the same numbers CI enforces. finops.rego also carries fin002_embedded_budget so that a bare `conftest test` with no --data flag still enforces something; that copy is NOT trusted to stay in sync by hand - tests/finops_test.rego::test_fin002_embedded_budget_matches_budget_json asserts it equals this file value-for-value and fails the gate if it drifts. Adding an environment requires BOTH a key here and a matching static clause in fin002_budget_max; the same test is what catches doing only one. Values are written with a decimal point on purpose: sprintf's %f verb refuses an int64, so a bare 250 would render as '%!f(int64=250)' - finops.rego's fin002_usd helper defends against that too, and has a unit test for the integer case. dev=250.0: the two synthetic Infracost breakdowns are ~$221.33/mo (single NAT gateway, matching the historical dev.tfvars single_nat_gateway=true) and ~$287.03/mo (one NAT gateway per AZ, 3 AZs); 250 sits between them, closer to the single-NAT baseline, so it accepts the conforming topology and refuses the wasteful one with headroom rather than on a hair trigger. prod=900.0: a PLACEHOLDER, not exercised by any fixture in this repo. Reasoning only: prod runs Multi-AZ RDS, db.t3.medium, a 3-node EKS group, a 2-node Redis replication group with failover and NAT-per-AZ (historical prod.tfvars), which scales the dev per-AZ estimate into roughly the $750-900 range. Revisit it against a real Infracost run before trusting it.
